notes: Core profile resources cover modern typed French identity, Latin-script orthography, Unicode punctuation, and a basic UAX #29 segmentation baseline.
Large corpus payloads are explicit forge acquisitions, not part of the ordinary language package.
The bundled distribution resources provide local Wikidata French core entity rows.
Wikidata French entity labels, aliases, selected relations, and canonical KB metadata are materialized locally for the declared extract scope.
The local extract is scoped and does not claim complete Wikidata dump coverage.
BCP 47 subtag registry resources are available for language, script, region, variant, grandfathered, and redundant tag consumers.
Lexique 3.83 provides French forms, lemmas, POS, gender/number fields, phonology, and source frequency fields.
This package is share-alike isolated and is not eligible for the default French composite.
CLDR likely-subtag, alias, and script variant resources are available for locale and script profile consumers.
Lexique 3.83 provides lookup morphology evidence; it is not a context-disambiguating analyzer.
UniMorph French lemma/form paradigms, feature bundles, lookup analyzer rows, and lookup generator rows are available under the share-alike policy surface.
Unicode/CLDR-backed NFC and lookup casefold policy plus Tatoeba-observed apostrophe, elision-prefix, contraction-surface, accent-fold, and gold-case resources for modern typed French text.

The executable search profile performs Unicode word tokenization, Unicode casefolding, and lookup-only accent folding. Lexique form/lemma data remains available through the lexicon and morphology slots and is not applied automatically by the search adapter.

The built-in adapter executes host Intl.Segmenter Unicode boundaries and applies the observed French elision-prefix table. Contraction, abbreviation, boundary-property, and gold-case resources are retained as quality/reference evidence rather than presented as executed rules.
UD annotation datasets are explicit forge acquisitions, not part of the ordinary language package.
Unicode 17 script, block, and property-value alias resources are available for Unicode profile consumers.
